the estrogenic effects of PFOA in rare minnow, a new fish model for environmental endocrine disruptor studies.
the effects of PFOA on estrogenic activity and reproductive toxicity in rare minnow.
the effects of estrogen-like activity in rare minnow exposed to PFOAs, which may have implications for the conservation of endangered fish.

PFOA is an endocrine-disrupting chemical (EDC).
the rare minnows are an appropriate species for the study of estrogenic activity of PFCs.

the estrogenic activity of PFOA is not only restricted to the liver but can also occur in gonad tissue.
estrogen-like activity of PFOA is a potential risk to the aquatic environment.
estrogen-like effects of PFOA were revealed by expressing hepatical estrogen-responsive genes in mature rare minnows, which is a good model species for studying estrogenic activity in fish.

rare minnows may be a good model for studying the endocrine-disrupting effects of PFOA.
rare minnows could serve as an appropriate model for investigating the effects of PFOA and other PFCs on fish reproduction.
